chunks: 4512 - Al-Sadiq عليه السلام was asked about the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic:
He said: "They are women who have husbands."
I said: "And chaste women from among those who were given the Book before you."
He said: "They are the chaste women."

key_terms.النِّسَاءِ: Women, specifically in the verse concerning prohibited categories in marriage.
key_terms.الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ: Those who were given the Scripture before the Muslim community.
key_terms.الْعَفَائِفُ: Chaste women, marked by sexual restraint and modesty.
key_terms.الْكِتَابَ: The revealed scripture given to earlier religious communities.
key_terms.الْمُحْصَنَاتُ: Women described as protected; here interpreted by context as either married women or chaste women.
key_terms.ذَوَاتُ الْأَزْوَاجِ: Women who have husbands, meaning married women.

ai.seo_question: What does al-muḥṣanāt mean in Quran 4:24 and 5:5 according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: Imam Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام explains two Quranic uses of the term al-muḥṣanāt. In the verse from Surat al-Nisa', it means married women, while in the verse from Surat al-Ma'idah, it means chaste women from the People of the Book. The hadith clarifies that the same term can carry different legal meanings depending on Quranic context.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.4512 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) was asked about the saying of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic: 
"And [forbidden to you are] married women" (Surah An-Nisa 4:24).
Imam (as) said: "They are those who have husbands."
I said: "And [lawful in marriage are] chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you" (Surah Al-Ma'idah, 5:5).
Imam (as) said: "They are the chaste women."
